title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: this is part of Grothendieck's 1986 attempt to axiomatize 'tame topology' (topologie modérée, Analysis situs). There is a set M of 'multistrates' (tame closed pieces, roughly closed cells or strata closures) carrying three relations:
- X <= Y, a combinatorial face / sub-multistrate relation;
- X << Y, the shadow relation, i.e. X is contained in Omb(Y), the closed set covered by Y;
- the compatibility relation 'not-crossed', written ≭ in the margin; X and Y are compatible when they can coexist in a common figure.
There is also a set F of 'figures of finite type'. Each F in F has a finite set F~ ⊂ M of multistrates, and figures are compared by <= (sub-figure).

On the previous page Grothendieck wanted G << F to mean 'G is a sub-figure of a subdivision of F'. He found this unnatural, even in the simplicial case. So here he simply defines (AE4/C4): G << F iff for every X in G~ there is Y in F~ with X << Y. The relation << on figures is thus derived from << on multistrates. He states the programme that the structure (F, <=, <<), or its abstraction, is to be reconstructed entirely from (M, <=, <<, ≭).

Axiom AE5 (C5): if X in M, F in F and X << F, then F^X = {Y in F~ : X << Y} (equivalently X ⊂ Omb(Y)) has a smallest element for <=. The set is nonempty by C4. Modern reading: every tame piece lying under a stratified figure has a unique minimal carrier stratum. This is the analogue of the carrier (support simplex) of a point or subcomplex in a simplicial or regular CW complex.

Reformulation: the family Multomb(F) = {Y~ : Y in F~} of shadows of the multistrates of F is itself a figure in M. C5 implies this. The two are equivalent if one also assumes that, for Y, Y' in F~, Y <= Y' (which implies Y << Y', i.e. Omb(Y) ⊂ Omb(Y')) is actually equivalent to Y << Y'.

This leads to axiom AE6 (C6): if X, Y in M are compatible, then X << Y implies X <= Y, hence X << Y iff X <= Y. In stratification language: inside one stratified object, 'lying in the closure of' coincides with the combinatorial face order. This is a frontier-condition-type axiom.

The next page draws the corollaries:
- In F~ the orders <= and << coincide.
- For compatible figures, F << G iff F <= G.
- Multomb(F) is the image of F~ under the injection X ↦ Omb(X), giving a 'shadow' embedding of M into P(M).
errors: No outright mathematical error. The labelling is unstable: the axioms are written AE4/AE5/AE6, the text refers to them as C4/C5, and the 'AE' prefixes are partly struck out.

The claimed equivalence between 'Multomb(F) is a figure' and C5 is stated only under an extra hypothesis (Y <= Y' iff Y << Y' in F~). That hypothesis is itself what C6 supplies, so the logical dependence is somewhat circular as written. It is sorted out on the next page.

ideas.what: Defining the relation 'G << F' between finite stratified figures by: every piece of G lies in the shadow (closure) of some piece of F. This replaces 'G is a subfigure of a subdivision of F'.
ideas.modern_name: refinement / domination of stratifications by closure containment
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in PL topology and o-minimal cell decomposition theory (van den Dries et al.)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only calls for a tame topology in general terms; these axioms are unpublished

ideas.what: Axiom C5: existence of a unique minimal carrier piece for any multistrate under a figure.
ideas.modern_name: carrier / support simplex (minimal closed cell containing a given set) in regular cell complexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical combinatorial topology (Alexandroff, Whitehead's CW complexes)

ideas.what: Axiom C6: for compatible pieces, closure containment equals the combinatorial face order. This makes each figure's face poset determined by shadows (Omb), so M embeds into P(M).
ideas.modern_name: frontier condition; face poset of a regular cell complex equal to closure order
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney/Thom stratification theory; regular CW complexes (Björner for face posets)

ideas.what: The programme of reconstructing the whole category of finite tame figures purely from a set of pieces with order, shadow relation and compatibility relation (M, <=, <<, ≭).
ideas.modern_name: axiomatic/combinatorial tame topology; compare o-minimal structures and Shiota's axiomatics
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries (o-minimality, 1980s–98), Shiota; Grothendieck's own call in the Esquisse

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out an order-theoretic axiom system (M, <=, <<, compatibility) from which finite tame figures are to be reconstructed. This is a purely combinatorial, point-free approach to tame topology rather than the o-minimal 'definable sets' approach that the community adopted. It was never written up or compared with o-minimality or with face-poset reconstruction results.
missed.quote: ces figures de type fini, (F, ≤, ≪) (ou leur l'abstraction) se reconstituent entièrement à partir de (M, ≤, ≪, ≭)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A point-free, poset-based axiomatics of stratified spaces could connect with exit-path / stratified homotopy theory (Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka) and with combinatorial models of tame geometry. However, the content on this page is close to known simplicial and stratified folklore.

deep.surprise_reason: The individual axioms (carrier, frontier condition, closure domination) are standard combinatorial-topology facts. The only notable feature is Grothendieck's unpublished attempt to make them the axiomatic basis of a point-free tame topology.
transcription_corrections: 'dans G ≪ F dès pour' should read 'disons G ≪ F ssi pour' (we say G ≪ F iff for every...).
'Voisin tub(F)' should read 'Multomb(F)' (multi-ombre), consistent with the next page; the 'A'/'b' is struck-through overwriting.
Under the definition of F^X the gloss reads '... X ⊂ Omb(Y)'.
The labels AE4, AE5, AE6 have the 'AE' partly struck out and are referred to as C4, C5, C6 in the text.
'prédominible' is uncertain; it may be a property such as 'irréductible' or 'prédominée'. The line '(C'est en tous cas impliqué par C5...' is correct.
The margin reads 'Cov / Omb(F) = {X ∈ F | ...}' (rotated), possibly defining Omb for figures via Cov.
